releases.notes: fixes for 9.13.0 found on the first car run:; Phone OTA in the car could leave the web UI wiped (recovery page): the safety gate was re-checked on every upload chunk, and one flicker of a CAN-derived flag mid-upload made the filesystem path erase the partition. The gate is now checked once, before anything is written; a firmware reboot is still gated and waits for the next power-on if the car is no longer safe. The sleep log no longer writes to LittleFS while a filesystem update is running; GET /api/busmon could truncate and take WiFi down: it buffered the whole body in ~40 KB of free heap. It (and /api/buslog) are now rendered in chunks from a small snapshot, with a low-memory 503 instead of a crash; /api/buslog/events streams from the file (?old=1 for the rotated one); About 14 KB of RAM back: 100-ID table (was 200), 12 h of samples (was 48 h; long history is for tower), smaller log task stack

Diagnostics: "Bus Monitor" card and GET /api/busmon. A passive census of every CAN ID received on each side of the controller (car / Haldex): count, rate, first/last seen, payload changes and last payload. Save a baseline (kept in NVS, survives OTA) and IDs outside it show as NEW, baseline IDs gone quiet as missing. Receive-only, works in every mode, and polling it never keeps the controller awake. tools/busmon.py reads, saves and diffs it; Sleep log (same card, GET /api/buslog): 2-minute samples of frames/s and active IDs per side for 48 h, plus an event file on LittleFS: boot (with reset reason), each side going quiet (and the IDs heard last), the ID that woke it and how long it slept, and low-power sleep/wake. Answers "did the bus really sleep, and what woke it" without anyone watching. `busmon.py log` prints it with wall-clock times

OTA: releases that don't fit this unit's partitions are no longer offered. "Switch to official" previously offered Forbes 9.00.6, which needs the 9.00.5+ Bluetooth layout (0x1C0000 app slots): on this fork's 0x1A0000 / 0xB0000 layout the web UI step would succeed and the firmware step then fail, leaving a mismatched unit. It now offers the newest official release that fits (currently 9.00.0) and says newer ones need a USB flash. Same check offered upstream

upstream fixes synced from Forbes-Automotive main (up to 4215b76, upstream 9.00.6), all by Kile Thomson, cherry-picked onto this fork's flash layout:; #51 a stopped CAN controller is now restarted whatever stopped it, and with CAN sleep enabled a no-light-sleep lock is held while awake. Automatic light sleep could power down the TWAI domain with the car running, leaving a controller stopped: no frames to the Haldex. Strong candidate for the Gen5 0AY "FWD in every mode" reports - on Luca's S1 (CAN sleep + aggressive on) the Haldex bus was seen to go silent while the chassis bus kept running; #45 Stock no longer feeds the reported engagement back as the lock command (latched high lock until FWD / power cycle). Stock now commands zero forced lock and forwards frames untouched; #46 when a bus goes silent, zero the inputs it latched (speed, pedal, ESP/hazard force flags, ABS valid, reported engagement); #47 default VAG correction factor matches its comment; Line endings normalised to LF across the tree, as upstream #49. NOT taken: upstream #44 Bluetooth LE / DashCAN and the new partition table it needs (app slots 0x1C0000, LittleFS 0x70000). A partition table cannot change over OTA, so taking it would force every unit - including ones updated only from a phone - through a USB flash. This fork stays on the 0x1A0000 / 0xB0000 layout so phone updates keep working. Upstream already carries #39-#43 from this fork

OTA tab: "Release source" switch between this fork and the official Forbes Automotive releases. On the Forbes source every stable official release is offered as a switch back (not hidden as a rollback), the install button and confirmation say so plainly, and the fork-only "Latest build" channel and rebuild check are hidden. Installing one returns the unit to the official firmware, whose own updater follows Forbes from then on; the hint and confirmation name the fork's website as the way back. Kept in this browser only; Phone install guide published at louij2.github.io/OpenHaldex-C6 (site/, deployed by .github/workflows/pages.yml): iPhone-only steps in English and Italian, download buttons that always point at the latest release, and official Forbes files for going back; The guide deliberately uploads FIRMWARE FIRST when coming from upstream 9.00.0. Seven different 9.00.0 binaries were published; the five before 16:04 on 2026-09-20 still answer "200 OK" after the first upload chunk (the bug 9.00.0's own changelog calls the root cause of OTA never completing) and write the filesystem while it is mounted, with no recovery page. On those, a cut-short firmware upload is refused by esp_ota_end and the unit keeps its old firmware, whereas a cut-short filesystem upload can boot-loop it. Firmware first means the filesystem then goes through this fork's fixed uploader

removed the dead "Generation 3 - Volvo" option from the Haldex Generation dropdown. There is no generation-3 code anywhere in the firmware and /api/settings rejects the value outright (API.cpp accepts only 1/2/4/41/50/51/52), so selecting it was silently ignored - a Volvo owner would read the option as support that does not exist; README: hardware badge said "Gen1 | Gen2 | Gen4" and omitted Gen5 entirely; the body text filed all of Gen5 under MQB when 0AY is PQ-based. Both corrected, and the badges now point at this fork rather than reporting upstream's release and commit activity; Dashboard now says WHY lock is being withheld. From 9.00.0 the speed/throttle window gates every lock path - the force-mode triggers and Expert used to bypass it - so an inherited non-zero "Disengage Under Speed" or "Minimum Throttle" silently zeroes lock in every mode and the only symptom was "Target: 0%". /api/dashboard now reports lockGated + lockGateReasons and the UI names the setting and its configured value. lock_enabled() is defined in terms of the new lock_gate_blocking() so the stated reason cannot drift from the decision actually taken; lock behaviour itself is unchanged; Release notes now come from this changelog (make_release.py reads the entry for the version being built) instead of a placeholder string, and nothing from a commit message is interpolated into a shell argument in CI. 9.10.0's own entry was backfilled the same way; Indexed the eight historical releases inherited from upstream (2.10.1 through 7.00.0) with real hashes, so `verify --strict` is clean and every published folder is accounted for. They are marked ota:false - documented and downloadable, but not offered for push-button OTA, since they predate the current OTA page and pushing one over the air would strand the unit's updater. Use Update from Files for those. The set offered to devices is unchanged

first release of the louij2 fork (MIT, upstream remains Forbes-Automotive/OpenHaldex-C6). Versioning moves to the middle field so our releases sort above the upstream cut they branched from and cannot collide with theirs; OTA updater now points at this repo, so devices running this firmware are offered this fork's releases; tools/make_release.py added: builds Releases/releases.json from the actual binaries, with `verify` (CI-enforced) and `reindex` subcommands. Upstream had no committed release tooling, and its index had drifted from the files - V9.00.0's firmware was re-uploaded on 2026-09-30 after the index was written on 2026-09-20 (+8576 bytes), and V8.00.3's entry was back-filled 192 bytes short. Both are corrected here, and `verify` now fails the build if the index and the binaries ever disagree again. Note upstream removed the OTA upload-stream SHA gate in 9.00.0 rather than fix this, so a drifted index was invisible to users; Carried the four PRs upstream left open: WiFi bridge mode / backup & restore / bench mode follow-ups (#40 CLI legacy key), favicon + PWA branding (#41), vehicle geometry settings (#42), and the OTA "Latest build" channel (#43)
